page: Microsoft Azure D32as_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dav6 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server features 32 vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with multithreading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable for external disk attachments.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core and multi-core capabilities. The D32as_v6 achieves top-tier performance in Geekbench single-core and multi-core tests, alongside strong results in text and image processing. Cryptographic operations are highly efficient, as shown by a strong PassMark CPU encryption score. Memory performance is also robust, with a PassMark memory score in the top 25% and uncached large-block read bandwidth reaching 79.93 GB/sec. For lightweight machine learning tasks, the system demonstrates strong performance in small-model LLM inference, processing 2668.32 tokens per second for prompt processing on a 135M model.

While the server delivers average multi-core stress-ng performance and standard database operations, the lack of local NVMe storage means disk-intensive workloads must rely entirely on network-attached Premium Storage. The absence of a dedicated GPU limits its utility for heavy deep learning training, though it remains highly capable for CPU-based inference. This hardware profile is well-suited for general-purpose enterprise workloads, including web serving, software compilation, text processing, and moderate database operations.
